title: Indian space startup SatSure raises INR 600 crore from government-backed space fund
summary: Indian space startup SatSure raises 600 crore rupees from a government-backed space fund
detailed: SatSure raised INR 600 crore from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund as part of its ongoing INR 2,000 crore Series B funding round.
The investment values the Bengaluru-based space startup at INR 8,700 crore post-money.
SatSure, the government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund, and regulator IN-SPACe are involved.
The funds will prepare the company's satellite imaging payloads for 2027 launches, support India's Earth-observation satellite network, and expand international operations.

Bengaluru-based space technology startup SatSure has raised INR 600 crore from the government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund as part of its ongoing INR 2,000 crore Series B funding round.
The investment values the company at INR 8,700 crore after the funding.
SatSure uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to support decision-making across banking, insurance, infrastructure and government sectors.

The latest funding will help the company prepare its satellite imaging payloads for planned launches in 2027, participate in India's proposed Earth-observation satellite network and expand its data analysis capabilities and international operations.

Bengaluru-based space technology startup SatSure has raised INR 600 crore (USD 7 million) from the government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund as part of its ongoing INR 2,000 crore funding round.
The company announced the investment on Friday.
The investment comes as India works to expand its commercial space sector through reforms that have opened the traditionally government-dominated industry to private companies and investors.
According to SatSure, the investment values the company at INR 8,700 crore (USD 93 million) post-money.
The Antariksh Venture Capital Fund has a total corpus of INR 1,600 crore and is anchored by IN-SPACe, India's regulator for private space activities.
The fund is managed by SIDBI Venture Capital, a subsidiary of the state-owned Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).
SatSure uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to help banks, insurance companies, infrastructure firms and government agencies make informed decisions.
Its subsidiary, KaleidEO, develops satellite imaging systems for Earth observation.
The company's ongoing Series B funding round comprises INR 1,650 crore in fresh equity, INR 250 crore in venture debt and INR 100 crore through secondary transactions.
SatSure expects to complete the funding round by December 2026.
The funds will be used to prepare the company's satellite imaging payloads for planned launches in 2027.
The investment will also support its participation in India's proposed Earth-observation satellite network, strengthen its data analysis capabilities and expand its international operations.
SatSure's existing customer base includes HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, ITC, Bayer and the Airports Authority of India.
Its technology is used across sectors where satellite-based information can support business and operational decisions.
The company has raised a total of INR 427 crore from institutional investors, excluding grants.
Its previous investors include Baring Private Equity Partners India, Promus Ventures and Asian Development Bank Ventures.
The latest investment adds to the funding available for SatSure as it prepares for its planned satellite payload launches and expands its operations.
Its participation in India's proposed Earth-observation satellite network will be an important part of its next phase of development.

The company's ability to strengthen its satellite imaging technology and expand its customer base across different industries will influence its growth as India's private space sector continues to develop.

Source Reuters
